rationale: The interview comparison requires ideas, evidence and credibility from two real interviews. No interview claims are reproduced for a filled comparison; a microphone photo would not teach credibility.
Light and darkness are explicitly interpreted as guidance and error. A literal beam or dark-room scene would confuse that figurative analysis, while a second text panel would repeat the explanation.
The Mutanabbi introduction links one life relationship to praise and pride but gives no dated event sequence. An invented portrait or travel map would not explain the selected poetic features.

The distinction is inner rhythm from repetition versus outer meter and rhyme. A sleep or music image would not demonstrate either; no full verse or verified scansion is supplied for rhythmic annotation.

Students select a descriptive verse and identify sense and rhetorical technique. An arbitrary pool scene would choose visual details before that evidence-based reading, with no full verse to constrain depiction.

The literary/historical comparison needs two accounts of the same period. No matched passages or dated events are supplied, so a timeline or portrait would introduce facts rather than compare the writing.
The exclamation-mark title asks students to discover what merits surprise in the story. A punctuation icon would duplicate the title, and an illustrated surprise would supply an ungrounded answer.
The narrative-technique comparison leaves the second writer and passages open. A portrait of one poet would identify a subject but not show how narration, description and dialogue differ.
Added a present-centred map of memory and wish, explicitly not the chronology of story events.

The lesson already names walking space, greenery, social contact and mental wellbeing. A generic ideal-city scene cannot show the expansion of a term; another labelled chain would duplicate the existing modelling explanation.

The astronomy task combines history, astronomical images and number graphics. No star-count data or named object is supplied for a chart; a space photo would illustrate only one medium without teaching synthesis.
The self-knowledge listening task compares speaker arguments. No personality traits or test results are transcribed, so visual types would invent content and bias self-description.
The visits-and-correspondence talk invites the learners own reasons. A selected social scene would imply one reason rather than support organizing their evidence and interacting with listeners.
The intrusive-person talk calls for tactful personal examples. A caricature would stereotype a person and would not teach evidence-led oral structure.
The beloved-city talk deliberately leaves the city personal. A supplied skyline would choose the learners subject instead of supporting the open presentation task.
The technology-impact talk does not select a technology or claim. A gadget montage would be generic proxies and introduce benefits without the speakers evidence.
The literary response lets learners choose between two poems and connect techniques to personal response. A scene would fix an interpretation rather than help students cite their selected text.
The short-story writing task leaves characters, setting and plot open. An illustration would constrain the sensory and figurative choices students are expected to make.
The persuasive writing task allows either city humanization or technology. A supplied conclusion graphic would choose a stance and repeat the organization already modelled.

The derivative-governance lesson already parses the subject governed by a participle and passive subject governed by a passive participle. Another arrowed sentence would repeat those exact analyses without new evidence.
Praise/blame components already have distinct cards and a fully parsed example. A person or thumbs-up image would identify sentiment, not the postposed grammatical specific term.
The exclamatory forms and indirect formation already have case-marked examples. An amazed face would repeat the communicative function while leaving the syntactic distinction unexplained.
Added near/far meaning branches for the exact example al-qusur, with context-based interpretation retained.
The depth comparison requires two actual text arguments. A shallow/deep water picture would literalize the evaluation metaphor; no source evidence is supplied for a filled table.

The lost-and-found story in the hadith already has an explicit event sequence and stated comparison. A desert/camel picture would merely repeat nouns; a divine emotion must not be visually personified.
Andalusian poetry includes nature, city elegy and eastern longing. A palace photograph would cover a setting, not explain all poetic features, while no specific passage constrains a scene.
Added an ordered vertical form diagram with recurring blue rhyme and distinct changing rhymes; explicitly not scansion.

The hail-as-scattered-pearls metaphor is already interpreted. Literal pearls falling from a personified sky would choose an image not grounded in a full verse and obscure the difference between natural event and figurative language.
Added a licensed actual samovar photograph, visibly an example, not the story prop. It resolves an unfamiliar concrete object without deciding its literary symbolism.

Classification, stereotype and bias are explained as a conceptual development. Illustrating groups of people risks reinforcing the stereotypes under discussion; another label chain would duplicate the existing account.
The age-based dismissal is explicitly analysed as attacking a person rather than an idea. A face or straw-man image would literalize fallacy names rather than add a new evidence relation.
The stress listening task evaluates advice without reproducing it. A relaxation routine would add unsupported health recommendations and pre-empt the speaker comparison.
The Andalusian-literature presentation leaves the work and claim to the speaker. A selected historical building would not teach supported literary analysis or oral delivery.
The poet presentation allows any Andalusian poet. An invented or unverified portrait would both impose a subject and distract from cited evidence and interaction.
The personal-experience presentation depends on a learner-chosen event that changed an opinion. A fixed scene would supply their personal content instead of teaching organization.
The research paper leaves the issue and sources open. A populated evidence diagram would invent a study or claim; the existing source and organization checklist supports the task.
The student CV task requires their own qualifications. A filled sample could invent achievements and implies a layout outside this imagery task; a generic resume icon adds no instructional relation.

The oath example is already split into particle, object and answer with reinforcement. An image cannot encode the grammatical relation and a second parsing diagram would duplicate the worked analysis.

The conditional example already identifies both jussive verbs and deletion of nun. A success scene would imply causation without showing inflection; another labelled sentence would repeat the case analysis.
The fa-linking lesson lists several alternative triggers. A causal flow would wrongly suggest they occur in sequence; existing separate category cards preserve the alternatives.

The emphasis example mentions angels and Gabriel. Literal depiction would be inappropriate, and a length bar would reduce rhetorical appropriateness to word count rather than the intended distinction.
The novel introduction invites predictions from pen plus named character. An illustrated girl writing would supply an inferred plot before pupils predict and invent appearance.
Learners are asked to draw actual character relationships. No names or relations are supplied here; a filled map would invent the novel network.

The task distinguishes narration order from occurrence order using the novels actual events. No event list is given, so a completed timeline would fabricate content or pre-empt the students ordering work.
Students classify technique in each chosen passage and compare another writer. A generic storyteller scene cannot demonstrate technique distribution without the actual language.
The pen symbolism changes with each appearance and is a target inference. A pen photo would repeat the literal object; a meaning-labelled picture would provide the interpretive answer.
Students draw the plot curve, locate the climax and predict resolution. A completed curve would do that assessed work, and no actual event list constrains one.
The critical response requires choosing a social issue and collecting evidence before inferring author stance. A supplied issue diagram would skip that selection and invent missing evidence.
The project permits critique, alternate ending or visual presentation. A model of one option would narrow medium and content choices; the existing plan-review-present scaffold covers all.
The historical/literary comparison needs matched childhood passages about Sheikh Zayed. A portrait would not reveal factual precision versus narrative feeling, and the passages are not supplied here.
Added paired hemistich versus variable line lengths. Blocks explicitly represent writing shape, not words or metrical feet.
The night is addressed as an emotional companion. A face in the sky would literalize personification; a night photo would not show the address or inner rhythm.
Students select the strongest poetic evidence for one praised trait and link it to history. A portrait or flag would identify the subject but not support that selection.
The child-dog relationship is read for compassion. A staged scene would invent age, setting and action, and could supply a sentimental interpretation before textual evidence is examined.
New s6d shows a hexagonal carbon lattice with atoms at vertices and the existing structure-properties-applications sequence; scientific lattice detail verified with NobelPrize.org.

Students build a scientific report from their chosen sources. A finished report diagram would duplicate the explicit title-question-evidence-conclusion-source structure without adding subject evidence.
The advertising listening task compares arguments; no actual advert or claim is reproduced. A product image would introduce a new advertiser and cannot establish source credibility.
The modern-poet talk leaves the author and work open. A selected portrait would impose content rather than teach organization, evidence and audience response.
The music-and-science talk leaves the scientific relationship unspecified. Notes and lab icons would be decorative proxies, and a waveform would require an actual sound to analyse.
The documentary talk does not choose a film. A still would choose the students source and add licensing and context assumptions without supporting their own analysis.
The response may address either praise poetry or personified night. A supplied scene would fix a response instead of helping students use their selected textual evidence.
The summary task may use a scientific topic or novel chapter. A filled topic map would choose content and reproduce the target summary rather than support accurate compression.
The chapter response asks learners to connect technique and ideas in a selected passage. No chapter evidence is supplied here for an accurate explanatory scene.
The lesson explicitly asks predictions from the real cover of The Falcon. Substituting a generic falcon or invented portrait would replace the evidence students are expected to inspect.
Pupils underline documented facts and artistic additions in actual text. A supplied depiction would blur that boundary without the underlying passages and historical sources.
Childhood councils are connected to later wisdom but no specific event or visual details are supplied. A childhood scene would invent appearance and setting, not evidence that causal link.

The dual biography/national-history timeline is the student task. No dated event set is provided here; filling one would introduce researched content beyond the imagery brief and do the ordering work.
Added a schematic channel/basin/farm distribution network grounded in UNESCO, explicitly no share quantities or portrayal of the fictional event.
The falcon stands for vision, patience and identity. A falcon photograph would repeat the literal subject and not teach how textual evidence supports the leadership metaphor.
The leadership relationship map is an explicit pupil task. Filling family, advisers and partners would supply the answer; no named characters are supplied for a reliable sourced network.
Students draw a challenge-consultation-decision-result chain for each actual situation. A generic second chain would duplicate instructions, while a filled one needs events absent from the model.

The union lesson compares emotion/dialogue with dated documents. A flag image would not show this genre distinction, and a historical event photo requires a matched textual passage for analytical value.
The event-year-trait timeline is the assessed organizing task. A completed map would select the evidence and infer traits for students rather than scaffold their independent collection.

The group newsletter requires students to distribute roles and design sections. A supplied finished page would constrain their design, while the existing named sections already provide the planning scaffold.
The final project allows letter, critique, film or presentation. A visual model for one output would privilege a medium and content choice rather than support all four.
